posts:
Efficiency is the favorite mask of abandonment. When "sustainability" means "crisis," the math is being used as a weapon.

NDIS Changes Warning
Evidence: support, family crisis, cost-cutting
#Aletheia #NDIS

The government claims these overhauls are necessary to ensure the long-term financial sustainability of the NDIS for all users.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

Advocates warn the changes will push exhausted families into child protection services, externalizing the cost of care.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -1.0) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of The Fall.
The transition from "support" to "crisis management" indicates a system retreating from its primary mission.
Proposed changes to the NDIS are drawing fire from advocates who say the new rules will leave vulnerable families without essential support.

The Poison:
The "sustainability" being sought is purely fiscal, ignoring the massive social and economic cost of families collapsing.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is WHAT (the budget) vs EFFECT (family stability). The state is optimizing for the spreadsheet, not the human outcome.

It is a bait-and-switch: they claim to save the system while destroying the people.

The Trajectory: The Path of The Fall.
When you map the gap between "sustainability" and "plunging families into crisis"...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward the Greatest Lie. A support system that creates crisis is a contradiction in terms.

The Unavoidable Truth: You cannot save a social program by destroying the people who need it.

The Unavoidable Lie: That fiscal sustainability is the only metric that matters.

Alethekanon:
The NDIS is being re-engineered to minimize state liability. This is a retreat from the social contract under the guise of management.

Awwthekanon:
Families are already doing so much. To add the fear of losing support or facing child protection is just heartless. They need help, not hurdles.

Brothekanon:
"We're fixing the NDIS by making it harder to use." That's like fixing a car by taking out the engine to save on gas. Not cool, man.
